Kernel: a now or a Lifecycle that cannot be read never raises out of a pull request's decide (#173) (#216)

The pull-request side of what decision 0034 did for an issue. A now that is no moment gives no
time to moved_at, so the wait shows as stale; a capacity deadline that cannot be compared with
now, either being no moment, defers the Run as capacity unread; a context that is no mapping says
nothing of the Pause or the passes. The limit is read by derive.overdue, one helper for either
kind of Work item: a Lifecycle not the item's, missing, or whose limit for the State is no finite
number of minutes shows the wait as stale, and an end the Lifecycle declares never does.
kernel/issue.py is left as decision 0034 left it. Four boundary tests, nine mutants each killed by
hand, three rows on decision 0034. Closes #173.

Identity hook: where the shell may stand, and a program it does not read may write (#213)

* Identity hook: a cd is placed exactly or loses the directory, a subshell's cd is its own, and a program the hook does not read may write (#174, PR B)

A cd, pushd or popd is placed only at the top level of a plain ;, newline or && sequence, as a
command's first word, with one operand, options the hook knows and no CDPATH set in the command;
any other cd loses the directory, so a commit, a push or a relative write after it is
directory_unreadable. shell.commands(scopes=True) now marks every subshell, substitution and -c
script with SCOPE, and what ||, | and & join with JOINS, so a subshell's cd is its own and a cd
joined by one is seen for what it is. cd - after a placed cd goes back to where the command stood.
In a command that commits or pushes, a program the hook does not read may write each word it is
given and where it stands; DATA_ONLY's words are data; find and tree join PATH_WRITERS.

Decision 0038 records it, with the triage rule for a finding on a hook pull request. Thirteen
mutants, one per rule, the writers' mutant rewritten, and two older ones follow the code they target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Identity hook: the fix round of #174's PR B, after Muse's read

popd, and pushd with no directory or +N, leave OLDPWD a place the hook does not know, so cd - after
them is read in every place the command stood in: `pushd <bad>; popd; cd -; git commit` was let
through, which main refuses. A substitution a quote holds that a program runs later, and an alias's
spliced value, are read with scopes, so a cd in them is that subshell's own. DATA_ONLY loses xxd,
awk, yq and sed, which write; tree joins PATH_WRITERS so its -o is read attached or bundled; a case
pattern is kept as a list so that a quoted | or ( is never read as a mark. Four mutants more, and
four older ones follow the lines they target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Decision record: the next free number at enqueue is 0039

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Identity hook: awk reads in place as sed does, and CDPATH is read only where the text names it

awk's operands are read, and written only with gawk's -i inplace, so `awk '{print}' .git/HEAD`
passes as before. The CDPATH reading parsed every command once more, which took the two long
readings past their bound; it now runs only where the text names CDPATH, plainly or through
quotes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Tests: two cases that tell the popd and the quoted-pattern mutants apart

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Decision record: 0040, since a hardening record never stands ahead of an exit record

Pull request 214 carries 0039.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Identity hook: CodeRabbit's counter-examples to decision 0040's rows, each a reading narrowed

A process substitution's ( opens a scope, so its ) no longer closes the enclosing subshell's; eval's
and env -S's scripts keep the marks of what they hold; CDPATH is read as the shell searches it, so
`cd .git` with CDPATH set loses the directory; only the suffixes of a short-option bundle that can
begin a .git component are read, so a long bundle is read in linear time. The rows say so, and name
gawk's --include=inplace as left to the boundary. A comment of #210's mutants gets its 0038 back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Decision 0040: the CDPATH row names no path token the context check would resolve

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Identity hook: the script-running built-in is one whose words are data, its script read as commands of its own

So a mutant that reads that script without its marks is told apart from the rule that the built-in,
standing in git's directory, writes there.
